title: Pomegranate culture
description: In India, pomegranates are grown almost exclusively in Maharashtra and its immediate vicinity.

title: Southern yellow watertanks
description: The yellow water tanks on rooftops in India are characteristic of the southern states—namely, Kerala, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka.

title: Bihar "kebab" fences
description: Those fences looking like kebab sekewers are located in northern Bihar

title: Brick kiln chimneys
description: Tall brick kiln chimneys, visible from far away, are typical of the poorer parts of the Ganges valley, especially Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. They are also fairly common in the poorer east of Tamil Nadu.

title: Wind farms
description: Wind farms follow the windiest areas: Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu have the most of them.

title: Flat roof tiles
description: Flat, rough-looking tiles laid like scales. Mainly Madhya Pradesh, in the centre around Guna, Sagar and Chhatarpur, and southern Uttar Pradesh.

title: Guna tiles
description: U-shaped tiles with a flatter tile connecting them to each other. Very common in south-eastern Uttar Pradesh and western Bihar, rarely in north-eastern Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand.

title: Flat Guna tiles
description: A tiled roof made only of staple-shaped tiles. Found around Prayagraj, in south-eastern Uttar Pradesh.

title: Wind turbines on ridges around Badvel
description: Wind turbines lined up on top of the ranges are very common around Badvel (Andhra Pradesh). It is the only place in India with big, dry north–south ranges both to the west and to the east, so even without turbines a good north–south angle points here.

title: Dry Andhra Pradesh
description: The area west of the north–south range is the driest part of Andhra Pradesh; with a dry landscape, click between Nandyal and Anantapur. Andhra is not as dry as Gujarat, Rajasthan or Madhya Pradesh, so be sure of the state first.

title: Red soil on the Andhra coast
description: Red soil combined with flat land along the Bay of Bengal, from around Ongole down past Nellore. Flat land, red soil and lots of palmyra palms should almost always mean the east coast.

title: Andhra coastal bush landscape
description: Flat agricultural land with coastal bushes, typical of the Andhra coast. Similar bushes exist in Gujarat, but Gujarat has holey poles, box cars and mostly date palms, where Andhra has palmyra palms.

title: Rocky desert between Dhone and Tadipatri
description: A rocky, desert-like river valley with only a few covered roads, between Dhone and Tadipatri (Andhra Pradesh).

title: Andhra bridge guardrails
description: Bridge guardrails made of vertical red, pink or orange concrete blocks with horizontal white or light yellow bars. Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

title: Thatched roofs in Andhra Pradesh
description: Within Andhra Pradesh, thatched roofs are found mainly south-east of Guntur, secondarily south of Nellore, and sparsely around Srikakulam.

title: Green pole stripes
description: Poles with green stripes, often combined with yellow or white ones, on the far western roads of Arunachal Pradesh.

title: Blue pole paint on the NH13
description: A section of the NH13 west of Roing (Arunachal Pradesh) has poles marked with white numbers on blue paint.

title: Red and white bollards
description: Red and white bollards are rare; in Arunachal Pradesh they are found mostly in the far west, in West Kameng.

title: Black and white bollards
description: Black and white bollards, not unique to Arunachal Pradesh, but most common on its foothill roads.

title: NH415, Arunachal's only divided road
description: The NH415 south of Itanagar is the only divided road in Arunachal Pradesh.

title: Mechuka car
description: A unique car in Arunachal Pradesh, found in the Mechuka valley and on the NH13 leading to it from Along.

title: White car with visible mirrors
description: A white car whose side mirrors are visible, in Arunachal Pradesh.

title: Tezu–Lohitpur road car
description: The car used on the road between Tezu and Lohitpur (Arunachal Pradesh).

title: Roing black car
description: A black car around Roing (Arunachal Pradesh).

title: Roing red car
description: A red car around Roing (Arunachal Pradesh).

title: Back antenna car
description: A car with a long antenna at the back. Mostly in Assam, west of Tinsukia and on parts of the NH15, and in Arunachal Pradesh around Tezu and Namsai.

title: Black car in Assam
description: The black car in Assam is quite central, its main cluster being near Golaghat.

title: Corn in Assam
description: Corn in Assam is found only between Nagaon and Guwahati.

title: Sugar cane in Assam
description: Sugar cane in Assam is found mainly near Lanka, south of Nagaon.

title: Thatched roofs in Assam
description: Thatched roofs are found mainly in the easternmost parts of Assam, rarely in central regions. In the west, tin is the main roofing.

title: Tea in Assam
description: Assam is the state where tea plantations are most likely in the north-east, mainly along the Brahmaputra in upper Assam.

title: White flowers in Assam
description: Bushes of white flowers that help find the right area of Assam. Not unique to Assam: use it only once you think you are there.

title: Andaman pole tops
description: Pole tops in Andaman mostly have vertical bars perpendicular to the pole. Not 100% unique, but very common there.

title: Over-saturated Andaman coverage
description: Andaman was covered with a camera with maxed-out saturation, which gives very bright, washed-out white colours.

title: Mongia Steel billboards
description: The Mongia Steel ads, a man and the company logo on a yellow background, are found in Bihar and Jharkhand.

title: Orange and black tiles near Madhubani
description: A cluster of wide W tiles in orange and black around Madhubani (Bihar).

title: Bihar huts
description: Three types of huts, mostly in western Bihar: clay "mushroom" huts in the north-west, huts made of sticks a little further south, and hay huts south of them towards Patna.

title: Clay houses
description: Clay houses are common in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, with some spill into south-western Bihar.

title: Stick houses with a layer of clay
description: Houses made of sticks with an extra layer of clay, along Bihar's northern border with Nepal.

title: Pineapple in Bihar
description: Pineapple fields in the far north-east of Bihar, around Kishanganj.

title: Tea in Bihar
description: Tea plantations are uncommon in Bihar, but appear in its far north-eastern tip, around Kishanganj.

title: Blue walls and tiled roofs
description: Houses with tiled roofs and blue painted walls are very common in Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh, a little less in Madhya Pradesh.

title: Dumka houses
description: Houses near Dumka (Jharkhand) have long tiled roofs and walls painted in two colours, green or blue above orange or brown. It spills a little into West Bengal, with metal sheet and thatched roofs.

title: Raised thatched platforms
description: Thatched structures on stilts, common between Hazaribagh and Ranchi (Jharkhand).

title: Jharkhand panhandle car
description: A car with an orange flag, in the north-eastern panhandle of Jharkhand.

title: Red, yellow and white bollards
description: Bollards in red, yellow and white (sometimes missing one or two of the colours). Jharkhand and Uttarakhand.

title: Date and palmyra palms together
description: Lots of date palms mixed with palmyra palms is one of the best clues for Jharkhand; Telangana has the same mix. Mostly date palms: think Jharkhand; mostly palmyra: think Telangana.

title: NH30 yellow lines
description: From Sukma to the Andhra Pradesh border, the NH30 is made of concrete and has yellow road lines (Chhattisgarh).

title: Goa cars
description: Goa uses three types of cars; two are unique to Goa, the third is also found around Daman.

title: Wind farms in western Gujarat
description: Wind farms are more common in the western part of Gujarat (Kutch and Saurashtra).

title: Southern Haryana
description: Southern Haryana looks like Rajasthan but still has the fields of the north: dryness combined with fields is a good clue for Haryana (or southern Uttar Pradesh). Northern Haryana is green and agricultural, like the plains from Punjab to Bihar.

title: NH3 between Zing Zing Bar and Killingsarai
description: Looks like Ladakh, with snow-capped mountains and lots of snow by the road. Unlike Ladakh, the front of the car is not visible.

title: Manali and the Kullu valley
description: Manali is one of the two covered areas in a recognisable north–south valley, the other being from Kullu to Nagwain. Manali has poplars and pines within the town, the southern area mostly random trees.

title: NH5 near Sarahan
description: This road near Sarahan has a double metal guardrail on its side.

title: NH3 between Gramphu and Dalang
description: Huge mountains, with a bit more green on their slopes than further north.

title: Spiti valley (NH505)
description: Very dry, very high, sparsely green mountains of unique shape. Unlike the paved NH3 to the west, the Spiti valley roads are unpaved.

title: Shimla roofs
description: The roads around Shimla have more bright green and bright red roofs than anywhere else in the Himalayas.

title: Shimla box car
description: Shimla is the only place in Himachal Pradesh with a box car, with its top right corner visible and a thread (sometimes not visible).

title: Jammu pole top
description: Very common around Jammu, but not 100% unique to it.

title: Jammu box car with leaning strap
description: A white box car with bars and its central strap leaning right. Common in Jammu, but also found around Sultanpur (Uttar Pradesh).

title: Jammu houses
description: Jammu looks more developed than most of India, with richer, nicer houses. Punjab looks similar in towns: without one of the two Jammu cars, click Punjab.

title: Kerala bollards
description: White bollards with a black and red band, in Kerala.

title: Blue and white bridges
description: Bridges with blue and white concrete guardrails are common all over Kerala (sometimes painted green) and in West Bengal; rarely also around Gaya, Bihar.

title: Communist symbols
description: Communist flags and symbols are common in Kerala, and also show up in Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Tripura.

title: Ladakh car
description: All roads in Ladakh have this white car with the front visible.

title: Snow east of Leh
description: Coverage east of Leh reaches very high roads, where snow can be visible.

title: Rock walls
description: Dry stone walls are very common around Kuno and Panna national parks (Madhya Pradesh), and in the south of Rajasthan.

title: Sugar cane hotspots
description: Regional sugar cane areas: central Maharashtra, south-west and north-east of Satpura National Park (Madhya Pradesh), around Erode and Tiruvannamalai (Tamil Nadu), and near Lanka (Assam).

title: White car with a back curving bar
description: A white car with a curving bar at the back, in parts of Madhya Pradesh and around the Yawal Wildlife Sanctuary on the Maharashtra side.

title: Rewa ridge
description: A fairly straight east–west range with a slight north-east angle, near Rewa in eastern Madhya Pradesh.

title: Slate roofs west of Sagar
description: Slate roofs are found west of Sagar (Madhya Pradesh).

title: Cotton around Nanded and Nizamabad
description: Cotton is found mostly in the middle and east of Maharashtra around Nanded, and in north-western Telangana next to it: click Nizamabad for a good score.

title: Imphal valley
description: Agricultural fields in a flat valley surrounded by mountains: Imphal (Manipur).

title: Western Meghalaya
description: Around Tura, western Meghalaya looks like Bangladesh with hills: hilly forests with areca palms and banana trees surrounding flat fields.

title: Western Meghalaya antenna
description: A car with an antenna on the top left, hard to see, in the far west of Meghalaya.

title: Mizoram light grey roads
description: Mizoram has light grey roads; many of them are under construction.

title: NH6 yellow poles
description: Between Aizawl and Champhai on the NH6, poles have yellow bands (Mizoram).

title: Mizoram back antenna
description: Some roads in Mizoram have a car with an antenna at the back: north of Aizawl towards Kolasib, and around Aizawl.

title: Grey car with double mirrors
description: A grey car with double mirrors, at the far southern end of the Mizoram coverage.

title: Green houses in Odisha
description: Houses in Odisha are often painted green.

title: Odisha roof mix
description: In Odisha, thatched roofs only point to the coast between Balasore and Puri; thatch mixed with W tiles, to the centre; U tiles, to the north-west near Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh. All three together mean the south-west.

title: Odisha bridges
description: Some bridges in Odisha have green and white concrete guardrails.

title: Conch shell party symbol
description: The conch shell is the symbol of an Odisha political party, often painted on walls with nothing else written.

title: Odisha flowers car
description: A car with flowers on its front, in northern Odisha.

title: Odisha box car with 6 indentations
description: A box car with six indentations on its roof, in southern Odisha around Malkangiri.

title: Odisha box car with 5 indentations
description: A box car with five indentations on its roof, in northern Odisha near Balasore.

title: Red car in Punjab
description: The red car in Punjab is found mostly around Ludhiana.

title: Dark grey car in Punjab
description: The dark grey car in Punjab runs along the Pakistan border between Firozpur and Amritsar.

title: Elevation in Punjab
description: About 95% of Punjab is flat; the hills are in the north-east between Chandigarh and Pathankot. Punjabi or a window pole with mountains: click there.

title: Dasuya forest car
description: The hilly Dasuya forest (Punjab) was covered with a car very unusual in the northern states; with Punjabi script or a window pole, it is a free 5k.

title: Haryal car
description: Haryal, east of Pathankot (Punjab), has a car unique in India.

title: Rajasthan shrub
description: A shrub with large pale leaves found all over Rajasthan, less in the surrounding states: lots of it is a good Rajasthan clue.

title: Wind farms between Jaisalmer and Jodhpur
description: In Rajasthan, wind farms are found between Jaisalmer and Jodhpur.

title: Western Sikkim yellow car
description: A yellow car (with or without antenna, sometimes almost invisible) gives western Sikkim.

title: NH179 spring antenna car
description: A car with a spring-like antenna, from Salem towards Chennai (Tamil Nadu).

title: Blue houses with W tiles
description: Houses with W-tiled roofs and bluish paint are 95% Tamil Nadu, the rest being spill into neighbouring states.

title: Thatched roofs in Tamil Nadu
description: In Tamil Nadu, thatched roofs are most common south-east of Thanjavur.

title: Chennai walls
description: Walls with this stone pattern are found in and around Chennai, though rarely.

title: Telangana rocks
description: Rocks by the road, boulders and rocky slopes are common in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, extending into Karnataka.

title: Black car in Telangana and Andhra
description: A black car (not a black-looking box car) is more common in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.

title: Gangotri road
description: The road to Gangotri has poles with red and yellow stripes and red/yellow/white bollards (not the only road with them). Its northern part often has snow-capped mountains.

title: Orange pole stickers
description: Orange stickers on poles, mostly on the eastern roads of Uttarakhand.

title: Yellow pole stickers
description: Yellow stickers on poles, mostly on the eastern roads of Uttarakhand.

title: Dehradun white stickers
description: White round stickers on poles, specific to the city of Dehradun as far as known.

title: Rakshasa masks
description: Households in Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu often place "demon" Rakshasa masks, prints or statuettes on the front of the house. Less common in Karnataka and Odisha, much rarer elsewhere.
